info.name: Buyer notifies order as paid

items.docs:
Buyer notifies that payment has been made.

- **direct**: Marks both pay_in_state and payout_state as PAID.
- **other providers**: Transitions pay_in_state to AWAITING_RECONCILIATION.

Optionally accepts a `file_name` field to attach a proof of payment document.

items.docs:
Returns payment orders for the specified provider.

- **stripe**: Returns orders (use /payments/service-fees/ for service fees).
- **direct**: Returns orders with per-order supplier bank details.
- **two**: Not yet implemented, returns 204.

By default, only DUE, OVERDUE, and AWAITING_RECONCILIATION orders are returned. Use the `status` filter to include PAID orders.

params.name: due_date
params.description: Filter by due month (YYYY-MM-01)

params.name: limit
params.description: Number of merged rows per page (default 20)

params.name: offset
params.description: Number of merged rows to skip (default 0)

params.name: order_id
params.description: Case-insensitive substring match against order_number. Order rows match their PO-XXXX number; statement rows match their own SF-XXXX invoice_id. A statement is NOT surfaced because one of its child orders matches — that match appears on the order row itself.

params.name: status
params.description: Filter by status (due, overdue, awaiting_reconciliation, paid)

params.name: supplier
params.description: Filter by supplier UUID. Applies to order rows only — service-fee statements are billed by Opply (not by a supplier) and are excluded from the response when this filter is set.

params.name: transaction_type
params.description: Restrict the merged list to one row kind. `order` returns only Stripe orders; `service_fee_invoice` returns only service-fee statements. Omit to include both.

items.docs:
Returns service-fee statements **and** Stripe (MoR) orders in a single response, paginated independently. Used by the buyer app's merged MoR table.

The legacy `/payments/?provider=stripe` and `/payments/service-fees/` endpoints are unchanged — older consumers keep working.

Filters apply to both halves of the response with the same semantics.

params.name: due_date
params.description: Filter by due month. Pass the 1st of the month (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: limit
params.description: Number of service fees per page (default 3)

params.name: offset
params.description: Number of service fees to skip (default 0)

params.name: order_id
params.description: Case-insensitive substring match against the statement's own invoice_id (rendered as order_number=SF-XXXX in the response). Child-order PO-XXXX numbers are NOT searched here — those matches surface on the order rows of the merged Merchant-of-Record listing instead.

params.name: status
params.description: Filter by status (due, overdue, awaiting_reconciliation, paid)

params.name: supplier
params.description: Filter by supplier UUID. Service-fee statements are billed by Opply (not by a supplier), so when this filter is set the endpoint returns an empty list. Statement rows belong to the unfiltered Merchant-of-Record view.

items.docs:
Returns paginated service fee invoices and Opply bank details. Overdue invoices appear first, then ordered by due date descending (latest month first). Default page size is 3.

Supports the same filters as `/payments/?provider=stripe` so the merged Merchant-of-Record view in the buyer app can apply one filter set across both halves of the table.

info.name: List suppliers for the buyer

params.name: include
params.description: Set to `ready_to_trade` to add the buyer's ready-to-trade suppliers to the order-derived list.

params.name: page
params.description: A page number within the paginated result set.

params.name: page_size
params.description: Number of results to return per page.

params.name: search
params.description: Search suppliers by name (case-insensitive partial match)

items.docs: Returns a de-duplicated list of suppliers for the authenticated buyer company. By default this is every supplier the buyer has placed an order with. Pass `include=ready_to_trade` to also add the buyer's ready-to-trade suppliers (those it can start a new order with) — used by the create-order supplier picker so a ready-to-trade supplier is selectable even before its first order. Supports search by supplier name.

info.name: Get Two credit summary

items.docs: Returns the buyer's Two credit summary. The `status` field signals which of four conditions applies: `available` (totals populated), `not_configured` (buyer has no Two integration), `revoked` (Two denied credit and recourse cannot compensate), or `api_error` (transient upstream failure — retry may succeed). When status is not `available`, all credit figures are null. `total_credit` / `available_for_new_orders` are the legacy additive model (Two organic + recourse) the frontend shows by default.

info.name: Merchant of Record app order endpoints

items.docs:
ViewSet for managing app orders from the merchant of record perspective.

This ViewSet provides endpoints for merchant of record companies to:
- List and retrieve their app orders
- Manage order lifecycle (approve, reject, mark as paid, etc.)
- Upload and manage order documents
- Create order events and comments
- Generate purchase order PDFs
- Handle invoice URLs
- Duplicate orders
- Create new orders

All operations are restricted to orders where the current user's company

ViewSet for managing app orders from the merchant of record perspective.

This ViewSet provides endpoints for merchant of record companies to:
- List and retrieve their app orders
- Manage order lifecycle (approve, reject, mark as paid, etc.)
- Upload and manage order documents
- Create order events and comments
- Generate purchase order PDFs
- Handle invoice URLs
- Duplicate orders
- Create new orders

All operations are restricted to orders where the current user's company
is the merchant of r

info.name: Move order to intermediate lifecycle status

items.docs: Transitions order to a target intermediate lifecycle state. Valid target states: order_received, order_sent_to_supplier, order_confirming_price.

MoR-facing viewset for listing, retrieving, and creating service fee invoices.

filter and `tab` parameter (all, pending, due, overdue, paid, awaiting_reconciliation).
Also supports `currency` and `statement_month` filters.

POST /: Creates a service fee invoice for a given buyer and month.
Auto-includes all eligible orders dispatched 2 months before the specified month.

params.description: Filter by the month the payment is due (YYYY-MM-DD). Filters on due_date.

params.name: status
params.description: Narrow the Outstanding total to a single status (due / overdue / awaiting_reconciliation) so the card matches the list's Status filter. The status counts always cover the full pending set regardless.

params.name: type
params.description: Restrict to one statement source. Omit to count both.

items.docs:
Status-count summary (overdue / due / awaiting_reconciliation) over the merged
service-fee + Two statement set, plus the per-currency Outstanding money total
(Two/grouped only, one bucket per currency, never summed across currencies).
Honors buyer / currency / month / type filters, ignores the tab, and is computed
over the full filtered set (never a page slice). An optional `status` narrows only
the Outstanding total (not the counts) so the card can track the list's Status filter.
